name: Locked CSPs
description: We introduce and study the random "locked" constraint satisfaction problems. When increasing the density of constraints, they display a broad "clustered" phase in which the space of solutions is divided into many isolated points. While the phase diagram can be found easily, these problems, in their clustered phase, are extremely hard from the algorithmic point of view: the best known algorithms all fail to find solutions. We thus propose new benchmarks of really hard optimization problems and provide insight into the origin of their typical hardness.
reputation: A classic theoretical benchmark family in computational complexity and statistical physics, widely cited for illustrating algorithmic hardness in clustered CSP regimes.
notes: Primarily a non-LLM, synthetic hard optimization benchmark; performance depends heavily on instance generation and solver class, and there is no single standardized score.
